cecfa85c4d.why: The judge's fix is in: 'though the wall carries no charge overall' no longer contradicts the key's 'the wall's opposite charges'. Key true (polarisation of a neutral insulator, nearer opposite charge outpulls the farther like charge); the three wrong choices (charge flows in, air pressure, a weak magnet) are real misconceptions and truly wrong. 'Overall' does not make the key workable from the stem: 'charge flows into the wall' uses the wall's charges too. No overlap: inside-the-atom (T4) keys atoms neutral overall, not polarisation; no T1-T3 unit asks a charged object sticking to a neutral one.

d843da3ea3.why: The high tell is gone: the stem no longer calls the ball a little Earth and no choice is 'Earth is a magnet'. Key true: Grokipedia (De Magnete) has the needle horizontal at the terrella's equator and perpendicular at its poles; Grokipedia (Terrella) has Gilbert suspending a pivoted needle over points of the terrella, the dip increasing toward the poles. Wrong choices (the reverse, level all the way, straight down all the way) are truly wrong and live; the answer needs the field shape, an 8th-grade field-mapping fact the lead's ruling gives this unit. Context checks: Robert Norman, mariner, dip 1581 (Grokipedia Terrella; NASA review); De Magnete 1600; Gilbert's latitude-from-dip proposal and its poor accuracy (NASA review). The North Magnetic Pole question no longer says the field points straight down there, so it hands this one nothing. No other final.json keys the dip or Earth as a magnet.

ee37ac9f0b.why: 'Judged by how magnets push and pull' is gone, so 'A north pole, since it lies in the far north' is live again; the 'points straight down' clause is gone too. Key true: the North Magnetic Pole is a magnetic south pole (OpenStax; Grokipedia). Wrong choices truly wrong; plain iron draws either end (NASA, Stern). No T1-T3 unit keys the compass or Earth's poles (T3 why-earth-supports-life keys the field shielding the air; T3 wegener keys field reversals).

4d2e8efc0b.why: The planted 'leaving the rest of the wire loose' clause is gone; 'a long insulated wire' still leaves wire to wind, and 'the same wire' keeps the current unchanged, so the key is the turns fact alone (ampere-turns). Reversing the battery only swaps the poles; copper is not ferromagnetic; the core makes the coil far stronger. T1's paper-clip magnet question keys revising an idea to fit results, and T1 telling-materials-apart keys iron, not copper; here copper is only a wrong choice. No other unit keys an electromagnet's turns.

77cd0e6e93.why: The joke choice is replaced by 'It lasts about a minute, as the coil runs down', the coil-as-battery belief, truly wrong (the field disappears when the current stops; a maglock releases instantly). 'If the power to the lock fails' closes the standby-battery gap. Three wrong outcomes (holds, fades over hours, lasts a minute) are distinct and live. No other final.json keys an electromagnet switching off.
